answer: Registration into the Atlas ledger requires a Wesolowski VDF seeded by the previous epoch's beacon, tuned to 6 sequential hours on a 3 GHz core. The prover posts a 2 KB proof, and any peer verifies it in 40 ms. Each identity locks 25 tokens, released only after the delta between its proof timestamp and first audited reply stays under 90 seconds. A 10,000 identity swarm needs 10,000 dedicated cores for 6 hours, about 60,000 core-hours, about $3,000 in cloud rent plus 250,000 locked tokens. Seniority accrues like cedar rings, one per season, and fertilizer cannot add a ring faster.
